Q: Opening MacOS terminals and running a command on each tab A:

If you're willing to use the third-party app "ITerm2", the following will do the job:

tell application "iTerm"
    activate
    
    set currentWindow to current window
    if currentWindow is missing value then
        -- make new window if none exists
        set currentWindow to (create window with default profile)
    end if
    
    tell currentWindow
        my runCommandInTab(tab 1, "echo Hello, World! This is a command in the main tab.")
        my runCommandInTab((create tab with default profile), "echo Hello, World! This is a command in a new tab.")
        my runCommandInTab((create tab with default profile), "echo Hello, World! This is a command in a third tab.")
    end tell
end tell

on runCommandInTab(theTab, theCommand)
    -- run the command in the specified tab
    tell application "iTerm"
        tell current session of theTab
            write text theCommand
        end tell
    end tell
end runCommandInTab

If you need to stick with the built-in Terminal app, you're a bit out of luck: Terminal's AppleScript implementation has been borked for a while, so we can't programmatically create new tabs or windows. However, you could (I think) achieve what you want by creating a window with tabs set up as you like it, and then saving it as a window group. You can then set Terminal preferences to open that window group at startup. I haven't tested that, though, since I'd need to know what commands you intend to run.

Q: Python: How to write jsonline without overwriting? A:

None of the solutions using the jsonlines module worked for me. However, I found a different module that does exactly what I need: the JsonLine class from the jsonline library. Here it is!

from jsonline import JsonLine
# dummy json
data = [{
"name": "xxxxxx",
"value": "xxxxxxx",
"domain": ".xxxx.com",
"path": "/",
"expires": 9999999,
"httpOnly": False,
"secure": True,
"sameSite": "xx"
},
{
"name": "xx",
"value": "xxxx",
"domain": ".xxxx.com",
"path": "/",
"expires": 999999,
"httpOnly": True,
"secure": True,
"sameSite": "xx"
}
]
jsondata = JsonLine('yourTextFile')
jsondata.append(data)
jsondata.append(data)
# To print the jsonline file
for item in jsondata:
print(item)

Hope this helps!!!.
